packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 12 - FIRST READING (image-only, unverified)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- No proposed identification of the work or author was given to me in my task context. I did not search for the text, did not consult any edition, catalogue or earlier transcription, and did not open packet.json.
- One deviation from the strict rules: I ran `ls` on the packet directory itself to get the image filenames. I listed or opened nothing else.
- The images themselves carry modern pencil shelfmark notes: image-021 has "Stams, StA, Frg. 242r" (the last character may be "r" or "u"), and image-036 and image-037 have "Stams, StA, Frg. 242v". I report them because they are visible. They name a holding, not a work.
- The main text names persons (see the transcription below). I transcribe those names as written. I make no identification of the work.
- All 42 images loaded. Overviews: image-001 (face A, the written spread) and image-022 (face B, the pastedown side). All the others are tiles.

=====================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY
=====================================================================
FACE A (image-001; tiles image-002 to image-021)
- Orientation upright. This is an opened bifolium (or a leaf folded at the spine). The fold is in the centre and shows sewing slits (image-004, 009, 014, 019). Each half has one column of about 33 ruled lines in a small gothic bookhand (textbook-like minuscule), brown-black ink, with frequent abbreviation.
- Left page: running text. At line 25 there is a red decorated initial "L" in the left margin (image-012), and a red rubric "De nomine" at the end of line 25 (image-013). The left margin beside lines 27-29 has a faded marginal note in a small cursive hand (image-012, image-017). Some words are faded or abraded, with gaps in lines 8, 9, 22 and 28.
- Right page: a top band of large later display/calligraphic letters in brown ink (image-005, image-006). It is decorative and I could not read it as words (see below). An oval paper label with a blue chain-pattern border overlies the upper left of this band and is inscribed "VI / L" (image-004, image-005). Over the first three text lines there is a large later brown inscription, apparently a number "[?] 1064" (image-005).
- Right page text starts with a large red pen-flourished "F" (image-004, image-005). A second red "F" is at line 13 (image-009, image-010). Red paraph marks (C-shaped) appear within lines 20, 23 and 27 (image-015). A red-boxed insertion is at line 13 (image-010, image-011).
- Outer right margin: red rubric "De nomine" beside line 1, with a 4-line marginal note in a small hand below it (image-006). A faint 3-line marginal note is beside lines 11-12 (image-011). Red rubric "De sco fran / cisco" is beside lines 13-14, keyed by a "+" (image-011).
- Interlinear additions: "penitus" above a struck word (left page line 7); "miracul'"? above "cōnotandi" (right page line 3); "ipe" above "pse" (right page line 7); several others noted inline.

FACE B (image-022; tiles image-023 to image-042)
- This is the other side of the same parchment sheet, used as a binding pastedown or wrapper. It is heavily overlaid with pasted fragments of PRINTED paper waste in gothic type, set at 90 degrees to the manuscript. At its edges are turned-in strips of a DIFFERENT manuscript in a larger textura with red paraphs.
- Through the gaps the underlying manuscript can be seen. It is the same kind of bookhand as face A, with red paraphs, and is a single column per page (image-029, 033, 034, 035, 038, 039; right-page fragments in image-030, 031, 035, 036).
- Much of face B is covered or abraded, so its readings are fragmentary.

AREAS SELECTED
- Face A: both pages, essentially complete (about 33 + 33 lines), plus the marginal rubrics.
- Face B: the visible underlying manuscript lines (left page, about 23 partial lines); right-page fragments; samples of the turn-in strips and the printed waste, kept separate.

UNREAD OR POORLY READ
- Face A: the display heading; the marginal notes beside the left page and beside right page lines 11-12 (mostly illegible); faded spots in left lines 8, 9, 22 and 28.
- Face B: everything under the printed overlays.

CONVENTIONS
- ⁊ = tironian et. ꝑ/p̲ = per/pro bar-p. Macrons are rendered as tildes or ¯.
- Expansions are in ( ). A "?" marks an uncertain reading. [illegible] marks unreadable text. [faded] marks text lost to abrasion.
- Line numbers on face A are counted from the top text line of that page as seen in the overview image-001. A tile reference after each line gives where the line is best seen, with its line number in that tile.

LIMITATIONS
=====================================================================
- Face A is well preserved and read nearly in full. The weak spots are: the faded words in A-L08 ("multis"), A-L09 (start), A-L12 ("ē"?), A-L22 (about 2 words lost) and A-L28 (abraded middle); the ends of A-R09 and A-R33; and the marginal notes, of which only the top-right one is partly readable.
- The right-page display heading is decorative script that I could not read. The "1064"-like inscription and the "VI / L" label are later additions.
- Face B: the underlying manuscript is mostly under pasted printed paper. I give only visible spans, and the starts of lines are lost under the overlay. The order of the right-page fragments is approximate.
- The turn-in strips and the printed waste are separate materials. My readings of them are low-confidence and are given only so they are not mistaken for the main text.
- I numbered face A by the overview's page lines, not per tile. Each line also carries tile references because the tiles overlap: lines repeated across tiles are the same text, not additional text.
- Suggested follow-up: a raking-light or UV view of left page lines 8, 9, 22 and 28 and of the margins. Images of face B with the printed overlay lifted, if that has been done, would recover the underlying page.
